business_problem: SkyAlert needed an infrastructure platform that could scale from low daily traffic to sudden earthquake-driven surges so alerts and connected safety devices would activate within seconds instead of arriving too late to be useful.
solution_summary: SkyAlert migrated its earthquake early-warning platform from Azure to AWS so it could scale instantly during emergencies and deliver alerts fast enough to help people act. The cloud design uses AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate to absorb abrupt traffic spikes without the long scaling delays of the previous architecture, while Amazon Pinpoint helps distribute alerts to large user populations. The platform serves both consumer apps and IoT-connected devices, so warnings can reach people and trigger automated actions ahead of ground shaking. By moving to AWS, SkyAlert created a far more elastic response system that sends millions of alerts in seconds, gives users additional lead time to take safety measures, and lays the groundwork for deeper monitoring and analytics improvements as the service grows.

solution_components.name: AWS Lambda
solution_components.role: Scales event-driven alert-processing logic during earthquake notification surges.

solution_components.name: AWS Fargate
solution_components.role: Provides serverless compute capacity so the alerting platform can scale without downtime.

solution_components.name: Amazon Pinpoint
solution_components.role: Distributes alerts to large numbers of end users.

data_flow: Earthquake events trigger SkyAlert's AWS-based warning workflow, where AWS Lambda and AWS Fargate scale processing in seconds and Amazon Pinpoint helps fan out alerts to apps and connected devices serving users in affected regions.
business_outcome: SkyAlert delivered nearly 2 million notifications during a June 2020 earthquake, now alerts millions of users within 8 seconds instead of up to 20 minutes, scales Lambda from 1 to 41 functions in under 10 seconds, and has given users more than 120 seconds to take safety measures.
